Definition: probably emphatic of G5100; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions):--every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.
BiblicalUsage: Who, which, what — the word opens the questions that run through the letters. Paul asks what man knows the things of a man, save the spirit of man within him, and John asks who is a liar but he that denies Jesus is the Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word earns its place by the questions it carries: the questions that expose what a man knows, and the question that names the liar.
